title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. About Mapandan The municipality History Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Geography Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 30.00 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2020 Land Area 30.00 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangays 15 DILG / Comelec About the Project What is Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Our Mission To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. How It Works We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is not an official government website. It is a community-run project that operates independently of the Local Government Unit. Volunteer-Run Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Get involved Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Report Incorrect Information Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Contribute Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → Verify Data Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Share with Residents Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Important notice Better Mapandan is an independent community project and is not an official website of the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

title: BetterMapandan.org — Mapandan, Pangasinan Transparency Portal
description: An independent, citizen-run transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan — officials, budget, ordinances, services, and emergency contacts, built under the BetterGov.ph BetterLGU initiative.
body: Independent · Citizen-Maintained · Pangasinan Mapandan, in the open. Officials, budgets, ordinances, and frontline services for the Municipality of Mapandan — gathered from public records and kept in one place, so every resident can find what their local government is doing. Browse Services See the Budget Find a Service Search every service Mapandan offers — by what you're trying to do, not which office handles it. Popular: business permit local hospital barangay clearance tax declaration 38,228 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Residents 15 Official Source: DILG / Comelec Barangays 9,326 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Households 1,274/km² Official Computed: 38,228 ÷ 30.00 km² Pop. density 30.00 km² Official Source: MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Land area Third-Class Municipality · Region I A rice-growing town in Pangasinan's third district Mapandan sits in the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan, bounded by San Jacinto to the north, Mangaldan to the northwest, Manaoag to the east, and Santa Barbara to the south. Covering 30.00 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership). 01 Founded Dec. 28, 1887 Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 02 Re-established 1909 A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 03 Agricultural heart Approximately 75% of the municipality's 30 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming. A Brief History The Story of Mapandan From a new pueblo to a growing community Before 1887 Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed, the area belonged to Mangaldan as southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, and Amanoaoac. Read the founding story Ten local leaders — Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin — led the petition for a separate town. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background Dec. 28, 1887 Mapandan becomes a pueblo Established as an independent pueblo through Director General No. 39, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. Read more The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan. Its administrative seat was first set up in Barrio Torres, then relocated to present-day Poblacion on land donated by the Aquino family. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1887–1890s The first town center The first seat was in Barrio Torres, near a church where Fr. Jose Torres served. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants. Read more The Torres location proved inconvenient — too close to the southern boundary. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had been a sitio of Apaya. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Torres History; Barangay Poblacion History 1903 The epidemic A severe epidemic devastated the municipality, causing population loss, migration, and fiscal insolvency. The 1903 census recorded 4,198 residents. Read more The epidemic directly affected Mapandan’s ability to function as a municipality, leading to its temporary return to Mangaldan. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile; PSA Census 1903 1905–1908 Return to Mangaldan Due to financial insolvency, Mapandan temporarily surrendered its municipal status and was re-absorbed as part of Mangaldan. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1909 Mapandan rises again Re-established as an independent municipality under Executive Order No. 10, issued by Governor General James F. Smith. Read more After years of demographic and financial difficulties, Mapandan was reorganized and re-established as an independent municipality, beginning a new chapter of growth. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1940s War and reconstruction The Second World War interrupted development across Pangasinan. Postwar years brought land ownership changes and community rebuilding. Read more In the postwar years, tenants gained opportunities to own land they had been farming. Communities like Sta. Maria developed from hacienda land into independent barrios. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Sta. Maria History 1965 Sta. Maria becomes a barrio Formerly a sitio of Luyan on hacienda land, Sta. Maria was established as a separate barrio, marking the growth of Mapandan’s community structure. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Sta. Maria History 1967 Golden becomes a barangay Formerly Amanoaoac North, Golden was established as a separate barangay. Named after the Golden Distillery that operated after liberation. Read more Golden underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, and cooperative organization. In 1972, it was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, with the award presented at Malacañang. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Golden History 1972–1973 Coral is established Created through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155, and Proclamation No. 11 (1973). Named after the stone coral enclosure built during the Spanish era. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Coral History 2002 Third-class municipality Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality, reflecting income and revenue growth under then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Physical Characteristics — Historical Development 2010s The Pandan Festival grows The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture, and community, held alongside the town fiesta. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Official Website 2022–2024 Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the Mapandan Super Health Center. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, serving residents of all 15 barangays. Read more The 2022 General Appropriations Act included &₱circ;6.5 million for the facility. Phase 1 provides laboratory and dental services for Mapandan and nearby municipalities. Source: Philippine News Agency, March 15, 2024; DBM General Appropriations Act 2022 2024 Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228, continuing to invest in public services and community development. Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, 2024 POPCEN Mapandan Town Plaza ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Population through time Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) Stories Behind Our Barangays 15 communities, 15 histories Each of Mapandan’s barangays has its own story of origin, growth, and community life. Sources & Historical Notes Much of Mapandan’s historical material comes from the Municipality of Mapandan’s official website, including the Municipal Profile, Physical Characteristics, and individual barangay history pages. Population data is from the Philippine Statistics Authority. Development milestones reference the Philippine News Agency and Department of Budget and Management records. Some barangay histories attribute parts of their narratives to “old folks” / local oral histories. These are labeled as local historical accounts rather than independently documented facts. Events include street-dancing pageants, trade fairs, and exhibitions of traditional pandan leaf weaving. Town Plaza Located in Poblacion, the Mapandan Town Plaza is widely regarded as one of Pangasinan's best-maintained civic parks, featuring an open-air auditorium, tennis courts, recreational children's playgrounds, and landscaped green space. title: Legislative Documents — BetterMapandan.org
description: Ordinances and resolutions passed by the Sangguniang Bayan ng Mapandan, plus the step-by-step process for enacting local legislation.
body: Sangguniang Bayan Legislative Documents Ordinances and resolutions passed by the Sangguniang Bayan ng Mapandan, and how a proposal becomes local law. Ordinances Recent municipal ordinances This list covers ordinances confirmed through provincial issuances and official municipal disclosures. More will be added as records are gathered. No. Title Key Date Status Source 5, S-2025 An ordinance creating the position of Municipal Government Department Head I (MDRRM Officer) under the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office Declared valid Dec 15, 2025 Enacted Provincial validation → 4, S-2021 An ordinance creating permanent positions for Tax Mapping Aide in the Office of the Municipal Assessor and Administrative Aide I in the Office of the Municipal Agriculture Approved Oct 4, 2021 Enacted Provincial review → — Real Property Tax penalty relief — implementation of Provincial Ordinance No. 253-2020 through the Municipal Treasury Office, condoning accrued interest and penalties on unpaid real property taxes Provincial ordinance, 2020 In effect Provincial Ord. 253-2020 → Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication. Provincial Provincial Resolution No. 272-2022 A key provincial resolution supporting LGU infrastructure cooperation. No. Title Date Status 272, S-2022 A resolution endorsing the construction and rehabilitation of farm-to-market roads and flood control structures under the Provincial Government's infrastructure program, including projects benefiting the Municipality of Mapandan 2022 Adopted Source: Provincial Government of Pangasinan issuances Process Flow How an ordinance becomes law The standard path a proposal follows through the Sangguniang Bayan, under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect within the municipality. Precedent A landmark case tied to Mapandan Navarro v. Court of Appeals (G.R. No. 141307, March 28, 2001) arose from a succession within Mapandan's local government. When Vice Mayor Baltazar Aquino assumed the mayoralty, the highest-ranking Sangguniang Bayan member elevated to Vice Mayor, opening a legislative seat. The Supreme Court ruled that the replacement had to come from the same political party as the vacating member, a precedent that continues to guide multi-tier local successions nationwide under Sections 44 and 45 of the Local Government Code.

body: Social Assistance & Protection Children in Difficult Circumstances (CICL) MSWDO protection services for children in difficult circumstances in Mapandan. title: Disaster Relief Assistance — BetterMapandan.org
description: The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes distribution of relief goods and financial assistance for housing repair.
body: Social Assistance & Protection Disaster Relief Assistance Disaster relief assistance for families affected by calamities in Mapandan. Relief goods and housing repair assistance available. Description The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes verification of affected families, distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC, and financial assistance (ESA) for families whose houses are totally destroyed. The MSWDO coordinates with the LGU, PSWDO, and DSWD Field Office I. Requirements Master list of affected families (from Barangay Captain) Barangay certificate Certificate of Indigency Procedure Report to the Barangay Captain the extent of damage. The Captain validates and forwards the list to MSWDO. MSWDO attends MDDC meeting conducted by the Local Chief Executive. MSWDO receives list of affected families and endorses to concerned social worker. Verification and inspection team (with Engineering, PNP, DSWD) assesses the damage. MSWDO requests and lobbies for allocation of relief goods from LGU, PSWDO, DSWD FO1. Distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC. For totally destroyed houses, MSWDO prepares project proposal for ESA funding. Financial assistance (ESA) is distributed to qualified beneficiaries. MSWDO monitors and evaluates project implementation for house repair/reconstruction. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: Varies (1 day for relief goods, 1–3 weeks for financial assistance) Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services AICS Assistance

description: Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. body: Real Property & Revenue Transfer of Land Ownership Transfer land ownership in Mapandan. Learn about the requirements, procedures, and fees for property transfer at the Assessor's Office. Description Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. This process involves coordination between the Municipal Assessor’s Office (MASSO) and the Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) to update property records and ensure proper tax assessment. The transfer may be due to sale, donation, inheritance, or other legal means. Requirements Deed of sale or deed of donation (depending on transfer type) Tax clearance from the Municipal Treasurer’s Office Valid government-issued ID of the new owner Original tax declaration Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) certificate of registration Procedure Secure a tax clearance from the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Obtain the BIR certificate of registration for the transfer. Submit all required documents to the Municipal Assessor’s Office (MASSO). Pay the assessor’s fee based on the property value. Wait for processing and verification of documents. Receive the updated tax declaration under the new owner’s name. body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Marriage License Apply for a marriage license at the Municipal Civil Registrar of Mapandan, Pangasinan. Description A marriage license is a legal requirement before a marriage can be solemnized in the Philippines. After publication, claim the marriage license from the MCR. body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Name Correction (RA 9048) Correct clerical or typographical errors in your birth certificate under Republic Act No. 9048. description: The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases.
body: Health Services Nutrition & Immunization Program Free nutrition and immunization programs for children at the Mapandan RHU. Malnourishment intervention and NIP vaccines available. Description The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases. The nutrition program includes assessment, deworming, feeding with nutrient-dense food, and monthly monitoring. The immunization program administers age-appropriate vaccines after reviewing the child's records and checking vital signs. Requirements Birth Certificate (Municipal Civil Registry) Medical Records, Vaccination Records (from hospital of birth or pediatrician) Procedure For malnourished children (0–59 months): Barangay Nutrition Scholar assesses weight and height. Physician refers to RHU for deworming and medical intervention. Child is fed with nutrient-dense food (high carbohydrate and protein). Monthly monitoring of weight, height, and alertness. For immunization: BHW interviews child's information and reviews records. Midwife checks vital signs (weight and temperature). Midwife administers age-appropriate vaccine. Midwife advises parent on child care and expected outcome. Schedule next vaccination. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 50 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Pre-Natal Consultation Day Care Program

Description The OSCA Death Aid Benefits provide financial assistance to families of deceased Senior Citizens. title: Pre-Natal Consultation — BetterMapandan.org
description: The RHU provides pre-natal consultation services for antenatal women. The service includes registration, physical examination, laboratory tests, health teaching, and classification of pregnancy risk level.
body: Health Services Pre-Natal Consultation Free pre-natal consultation for antenatal women at the Mapandan Rural Health Unit. Lab tests and health teaching included. Description The RHU provides pre-natal consultation services for antenatal women. The service includes registration in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR), OB history, vital signs, Leopold's maneuver, fetal heartbeat assessment, and fundic height measurement. The MHO conducts complete physical examination, interprets laboratory results, and provides health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. High-risk patients are referred to higher-level facilities. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Laboratory Results, Prescription for Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Procedure Register in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Midwife encodes OB history, vital signs, and performs Leopold's maneuver. Request for routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg Screening, RPR test). MHO performs complete physical examination and interprets laboratory results. If high-risk, patient is referred to a higher level of facility. Health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 55 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation Family Planning

body: Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications PWD Assistive Devices Request assistive devices for PWDs from the MSWDO in Mapandan. Crutches, wheelchairs, and other devices available. Description The MSWDO provides assistive devices such as crutches, wheelchairs, prosthesis, and other gadgets to Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) to help them integrate into the mainstream of community life. title: Rabies Treatment — BetterMapandan.org
description: The RHU provides anti-rabies treatment for animal bite patients. The service includes wound assessment, counselling, vaccination, and post-treatment instructions. First dose is free for Mapandan residents and 4P's members.
body: Health Services Rabies Treatment Free rabies treatment for animal bite patients at the Mapandan RHU Animal Bite Treatment Center. First dose free for residents. Description The RHU provides anti-rabies treatment for animal bite patients through the Animal Bite Treatment Center (ABTC). The service includes wound assessment, counselling, prescription of rabies vaccine or immunoglobulin, and post-treatment instructions. The first dose is free for 4P's members and Mapandan residents. Subsequent doses cost ₱350 each. Requirements Rabies exposure case (bite or scratch) Procedure Register in the log book. Midwife classifies patient (new/old, PhilHealth member, emergency/senior citizen priority). Record patient's data, vital signs, and bite/scratch details. MHO performs wound/scratch assessment and provides counselling. MHO prescribes rabies vaccine or immunoglobulin (as applicable). ABTC Nurse administers anti-rabies vaccine and/or immunoglobulin. ABTC Nurse provides post-treatment instructions and follow-up schedule. Pharmacy Assistant dispenses vaccines or medicine. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 37 minutes per client Fee: Free (1st dose for Mapandanians and 4P's members); ₱350 for subsequent doses Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit (ABTC), Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation Laboratory Examination

body: Health Services Sanitary Permit Get a sanitary permit, health certificate, or medical certificate at the Mapandan RHU. 53 minutes processing time. Description A sanitary permit is required for all businesses that handle food, beverages, or other consumable products to ensure compliance with health and sanitation standards. The permit is issued by the Municipal Health Office (MHO) after an inspection of the business premises to verify that health and safety regulations are met. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Laboratory Tests: CBC, urinalysis, fecalysis, sputum exam, Hepatitis B (from RHU Primary Laboratory) Chest X-Ray, PA (from government or private diagnostic facility) Procedure Present official receipt from the Treasury Office. List down certificate number on logbook and release certification (2 min). title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. body: Support Frequently Asked Questions Answers to common questions about government services and civic information in Mapandan. General About Better Mapandan Is this an official government website? No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .
